The heart is the root of the midot, and linking the heart's desire (חפץ) to the da'at-cluster (Package 1) is the Torah's own exegesis of Psalm 34:13: 'מִי הָאִישׁ הֶחָפֵץ חַיִּים' — whose desire (חפץ = heart) for life (חיים = da'at) ties the lev to da'at.

The Torah as shalom and the tzaddikim as brit-shalom are both expressions of the same inner reality: the ahavah-she-b'da'at when revealed produces shalom. Shalom is explicitly equated with the revealed state of Torah and the tzaddik. It belongs in Package 1 as the relational/harmonious face of the good cluster.
